harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: On node1, /srv/data was converted into a btrfs subvolume (backed by a loop-mounted image file, since root is plain ext4 with no spare disk/LVM) to enable true filesystem snapshots. Baseline application data was written, snapshotted read-only (snap-baseline), then the live directory was corrupted (file edited, file deleted, stray file added). Restore was performed by creating a writable snapshot of snap-baseline and swapping it in as the live /data subvolume mounted at /srv/data — verified via SHA-256 hashes matching the pre-corruption baseline exactly. Mandatory reboot evidence: captured pre-restart boot_id, issued `shutdown -r now`, polled until reconnect, confirmed boot_id changed, and reconfirmed /srv/data auto-remounted (via fstab) with identical file content/hashes and all btrfs subvolumes (data, snapshots/snap-baseline, corrupted subvolume) intact post-reboot.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 storage: single ext4 root disk, no LVM/spare disk
Created 2G loopback-backed btrfs image at /var/lib/srv-data-backing/srv-data.img
Created btrfs subvolume 'data', mounted it at /srv/data via /etc/fstab (loop,subvol=data)
Wrote baseline app data (app.conf, records.csv, uploads/file1.txt) and recorded SHA-256 hashes
Created read-only snapshot 'snap-baseline' of /srv/data
Modified /srv/data: changed app.conf, deleted records.csv, added junk.txt; confirmed change via hashes
Restored /srv/data by unmounting, creating writable snapshot of snap-baseline, swapping it in as the 'data' subvolume, remounting
Verified restored file hashes exactly match pre-modification baseline
Captured pre-restart boot_id and mount/data state
Rebooted node1 via 'shutdown -r now' (backgrounded so ack returned before disconnect)
Polled node1 until exec access returned
Verified boot_id changed, confirming actual restart
Verified /srv/data auto-remounted post-reboot with identical file hashes and all btrfs subvolumes intact

evidence.requirement: Baseline data captured under /srv/data before snapshot
evidence.summary: Listed files and SHA-256 hashes for app.conf, records.csv, uploads/file1.txt immediately after writing baseline data

evidence.requirement: Snapshot taken via native filesystem mechanism (btrfs)
evidence.summary: Created read-only btrfs snapshot 'snap-baseline' of the /srv/data subvolume; btrfs subvolume list shows both subvolumes
app.conf overwritten with different content, records.csv deleted, junk.txt added; hashes differ from baseline
Swapped live subvolume for a writable snapshot of snap-baseline and remounted /srv/data; post-restore hashes for all three files exactly match the original baseline hashes

evidence.requirement: Healthy baseline (boot identity + data health) captured before restart
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 901ef286-c79c-44c0-ad2c-cfde1f6daa7a, confirmed /srv/data mount and matching file hashes prior to reboot
Issued 'shutdown -r now' in background; command stream closed as node went down, consistent with acknowledged reboot

evidence.requirement: Proof boot identity changed after restart
evidence.summary: Polling failed while node was down, then succeeded with new boot_id a960268e-c556-42c9-879d-bd934ac25d6e, differing from pre-restart boot_id

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required services/data verified
evidence.summary: After reboot, /srv/data auto-remounted via fstab (subvolid=258) with file hashes identical to the restored baseline, and btrfs subvolume list shows data, snapshots/snap-baseline, and the corrupted subvolume all intact
